tweets: Mīnākṣī—the fish-eyed goddess—watches over Madurai from her temple's fourteen gopurams, gateway towers rising in painted tiers that carry an estimated 33,000 sculpted figures: gods, sages, and beasts frozen mid-procession.

The towers date largely to 17th-century patronage of Thirumalai Nayak, though the shrine is far older, sung of in early Tamil poetry. Nearby stands his Thousand Pillar Hall, 985 carved columns. Follow @yddoseOfHistory for your daily dose of history.
